rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers among the People of the Book do not conceal their knowledge for payment; they disclose it freely and receive reward from God, who reckons swiftly.
rows.anchor: بل يبذلون ذلك مجانا؛ ولهذا قال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses God's swift reckoning as swift enumeration; Ibn Abi Hatim and others transmit this interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: {سريع الحساب} يعني: سريع الإحصاء.

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says believers must remain steadfast in Islam through ease and hardship until death, and persevere against enemies who conceal their religion; other early scholars agree.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن البصري، رحمه الله: أمروا أن يصبروا على دينهم الذي ارتضاه الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat can mean persisting and remaining firm in a place of worship.
rows.anchor: وأما المرابطة فهي المداومة في مكان العبادة والثبات.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, Sahl ibn Hunayf, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others explain ribat as waiting for one prayer after another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة، قاله [مجاهد و] (11) ابن عباس وسهل بن حنيف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that completing ablution despite difficulty, walking often to mosques, and waiting between prayers erase sins and raise ranks; these acts are called ribat.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ألا أخبركم بما يمحو الله به الخطايا، ويرفع به الدرجات

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse addressed people who maintained mosque prayers on time and remembered God there: endure the five prayers, resist the self and desires, and remain in mosques.
rows.anchor: أقبل علي أبو هريرة يوما فقال: أتدري يا ابن أخي فيم نزلت

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Hakim transmits a route corroborating Abu Hurayra's report that the verse's ribat was waiting between prayers because there was no wartime frontier post in the Prophet's era.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة -بنحوه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports the Prophet's teaching that thorough ablution in difficulty and waiting from prayer to prayer expiate sins; this is ribat.
rows.anchor: عن شرحبيل، عن علي، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا أدلكم على ما يكفر الذنوب والخطايا؟

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet listing thorough ablution, many steps to mosques, and waiting between prayers as expiation of sins and ribat.
rows.anchor: عن شرحبيل، عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Ayyub reports the Prophet identifying ablution, frequent mosque walks, and waiting between prayers as ribat in mosques, explicitly linking them to this verse; Ibn Kathir calls this route very unusual.
rows.anchor: قال: "وهو قول الله تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون} فذلك هو الرباط في المساجد"

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama says the verse did not concern military frontier posts in the Prophet's time but waiting from one prayer to the next; Ibn Kathir notes the earlier version is Abu Hurayra's wording, God knows best.
rows.anchor: قال لي أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: يا ابن أخي، هل تدري في أي شيء نزلت هذه الآية {اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is military ribat: guarding Islam's frontiers against enemy entry, for which reports promise abundant reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالمرابطة هاهنا مرابطة الغزو في نحور العدو، وحفظ ثغور الإسلام وصيانتها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi reports the Prophet saying one day stationed in God's cause is better than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي، رضي الله عنه (3) أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "رباط يوم في سبيل الله خير من الدنيا وما عليها"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Salman reports that a day and night of ribat surpass a month of fasting and prayer; if the guard dies there, his deeds and provision continue and he is safe from the testers.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي، عن رسوله الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "رباط يوم وليلة خير من صيام شهر وقيامه، وإن مات جرى عليه عمله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Fadala ibn Ubayd reports that a martyr's deeds cease except for one who dies guarding the frontier, whose deeds grow until resurrection and who is spared the grave trial; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: أنه سمع فضالة بن عبيد يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كل ميت يختم على عمله، إلا الذي مات مرابطا في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Lahi'a's explicit transmission is acceptable, especially when supported by the preceding corroborating reports.
rows.anchor: وابن لهيعة إذا صرح بالتحديث فهو حسن، ولا سيما مع ما تقدم من الشواهد.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that a frontier guard's deeds continue until resurrection and he is protected from the testers; Ibn Mardawayh also transmits a shorter version omitting that protection.
rows.anchor: سمعت عقبة بن عامر يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كل ميت يختم له على عمله، إلا المرابط في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that one dying in ribat keeps receiving his righteous deeds and provision, is safe from the testers, and rises secure from the great terror.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من مات مرابطا في سبيل الله، أجري (7) عليه عمله الصالح الذي كان يعمل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another Abu Hurayra report says the deceased guard is protected from the grave trial and greatest terror, receives Paradise's provision morning and evening, and earns ribat's reward until resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من مات مرابطا وقي فتنة القبر، وأمن (9) من الفزع الأكبر

rows.speaker: أم الدرداء
rows.claim: Umm al-Darda raises a report that three days guarding any Muslim coastline suffice as a year of ribat.
rows.anchor: عن أم الدرداء ترفع الحديث قالت (11) من رابط في شيء من سواحل المسلمين ثلاثة أيام، أجزأت عنه رباط سنة

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman reports from the Prophet that one night guarding in God's cause is better than a thousand nights spent in prayer and fasting.
rows.anchor: قال عثمان، رضي الله عنه -وهو يخطب على منبره-: إني محدثكم حديثا سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: A second Uthman transmission says one night of ribat equals a thousand nights of fasting and standing in worship.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: خطب عثمان بن عفان الناس فقال: يأيها الناس، إني سمعت حديثا من رسول الله

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman reports that one day of ribat in God's cause is better than a thousand days elsewhere; al-Tirmidhi grades this route hasan gharib.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح مولى عثمان بن عفان قال: سمعت عثمان -وهو على المنبر-يقول: إني كتمتكم حديثا

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Ahmad's version adds Uthman's invitation to choose whether to serve at the frontier, followed by his asking God to witness that he conveyed the report.
rows.anchor: فقال -يعني عثمان-: فليرابط امرؤ كيف شاء، هل بلغت؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: اللهم اشهد

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: Salman tells Shurahbil that one day of ribat exceeds a month of fasting and prayer, and that death there brings protection from the grave trial and continuing deeds; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan.
rows.anchor: مر سلمان الفارسي بشرحبيل بن السمط، وهو في مرابط له، وقد شق عليه وعلى أصحابه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Although some copies say Ibn al-Munkadir's chain from Salman is disconnected, Ibn Kathir thinks he heard it from Shurahbil; Muslim and al-Nasa'i transmit corroborating routes through Shurahbil, Salman, and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض النسخ زيادة: وليس إسناده بمتصل، وابن المنكدر لم يدرك سلمان.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b's report promises immense reward for guarding a Muslim vulnerable frontier: a day outside Ramadan equals a hundred years of worship and a Ramadan day a thousand; the returning guard remains sinless and earns ribat reward until Judgment. Ibn Kathir calls this route gharib and munkar, and its transmitter Umar ibn Subayh accused.
rows.anchor: عن مكحول، عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لرباط يوم في سبيل الله، من وراء عورة المسلمين محتسبا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports one night of guarding surpasses a man's thousand years of fasting and worship at home, counting a year as 360 days; Ibn Kathir calls it gharib and notes Sa'id ibn Khalid was weakened and accused of unsupported and fabricated reports.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن خالد بن أبي طويل، سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "حرس ليلة في سبيل الله أفضل من صيام رجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report asks God to show mercy to the sentry; Ibn Kathir notes a broken link because Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz did not meet Uqba ibn Amir.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز، عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "رحم الله حارس الحرس"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Hunayn, Anas ibn Abi Mirthad volunteers to guard a mountain pass overnight after a scout reports Hawazin assembled there; he returns by morning and the Prophet says his service has earned its reward.
rows.anchor: حدثه سهل ابن الحنظلية (7) أنهم ساروا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم حنين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: On a cold campaign night, Abu Rayhana recounts the Prophet praying extensively for an Ansari volunteer who guarded, then more briefly for Abu Rayhana; the Prophet says fire is forbidden to an eye weeping from God's fear or kept awake in God's cause.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا ريحانة يقول: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i transmits Abu Rayhana's report that fire is forbidden to eyes that weep from fear of God or keep vigil in God's cause, through routes naming Abu Ali al-Janbi.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي منه: "حرمت النار ... " إلى آخره عن عصمة بن الفضل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that two eyes will not be touched by fire: one weeping in fear of God and one keeping watch in God's cause; al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan gharib and says it is known only through Shu'ayb ibn Ruzayq.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "عينان لا تمسهما النار: عين بكت من خشية الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Mu'adh ibn Anas reports that a volunteer who guards Muslims without a ruler's wage will not see the Fire except for the passage required by the oath; Ahmad alone transmits it, and it cites the universal passage over Hell.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه معاذ بن أنس، رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من حرس من وراء المسلمين في سبيل الله متطوعا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra's report contrasts the resentful servant of money and fine clothes with the rough, dusty horseman in God's cause, content to guard or serve in the rear and without status.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " تعس عبد الدينار وعبد الدرهم وعبد الخميصة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In a letter encouraging Abu Ubayda amid Roman forces, Umar says hardship for a believer is followed by relief and cites this verse, adding that one hardship will not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: فكتب إليه عمر: أما بعد فإنه مهما ينزل بعبد مؤمن من منزلة شدة يجعل الله بعدها فرجا

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak's Tarsus poem to al-Fudayl contrasts worship in the holy sanctuaries with frontier service: fighters shed blood, endure dust and heat, and cite the Prophet and Qur'an for the martyr's merit; al-Fudayl weeps and calls it sincere counsel.
rows.anchor: قال: أملى علي عبد الله بن المبارك هذه الأبيات بطرسوس، وودعته للخروج

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a man unable to sustain uninterrupted prayer and fasting asks how to earn fighters' reward; the Prophet says he could not match them and even a campaigning horse earns good deeds while exercising at its tether.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله علمني عملا أنال به ثواب المجاهدين في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-consciousness is required in every affair and circumstance; the Prophet advised Mu'adh to fear God everywhere, follow a bad deed with a good one, and treat people well.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {واتقوا الله} أي: في جميع أموركم وأحوالكم، كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ [بن جبل]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of flourishing means success in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: {لعلكم تفلحون} أي: في الدنيا والآخرة.

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses the command as fearing God in what lies between Him and people, so they may succeed when they meet Him tomorrow.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي: أنه كان يقول في قول الله عز وجل: {واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون} واتقوا الله فيما بيني وبينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse bars incompetent people from managing wealth that sustains livelihoods; guardianship may be imposed for minority, insanity, deficient judgment or religion, and insolvency after creditors seek a court order.
rows.anchor: أي: تقوم (3) بها معايشهم من التجارات وغيرها. ومن هاهنا يؤخذ الحجر على السفهاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to identify the incompetent as one's sons and women; al-Dahhak likewise explains them as women and children.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم} قال: هم بنوك والنساء

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr interprets the incompetent referred to here as orphans.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هم اليتامى.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ikrima, and Qatada interpret the incompetent as women.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة وقتادة: هم النساء.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports a saying that women are incompetent except one who obeys her financial guardian; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits it and Ibn Mardawayh gives a longer version.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "وإن النساء السفهاء إلا التي أطاعت قيمها"

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra explains the incompetent as servants, calling them human devils; Ibn Kathir cites the report without endorsing its wording.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة {ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم} قال: الخدم، وهم شياطين الإنس وهم الخدم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says guardians should retain and manage their livelihood wealth rather than hand it to wives or children and then depend on their funds; the guardian should provide their clothing, maintenance, and provisions.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس يقول [تعالى] (9) لا تعمد إلى مالك وما خولك الله

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa names three unanswered supplications: against an unkind wife one refuses to divorce, after giving wealth to an incompetent person, and over an undocumented loan.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال: ثلاثة يدعون الله فلا يستجيب لهم: رجل كانت له امرأة سيئة الخلق فلم يطلقها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains speaking in a recognized good manner as kindness and maintaining family ties.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {وقولوا لهم قولا معروفا} يعني في البر والصلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage joins practical generosity to family and dependents under guardianship with clothing, support, kind speech, and good conduct.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية الكريمة انتظمت الإحسان إلى العائلة، ومن تحت الحجر بالفعل، من الإنفاق في الكساوى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan say guardians should test the orphans before handing over their wealth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والحسن، والسدي، ومقاتل بن حيان: أي اختبروهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses reaching marriageable age as reaching puberty.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني: الحلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars say a boy reaches puberty through a wet dream and emission of semen capable of producing a child.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور من العلماء: البلوغ في الغلام تارة يكون بالحلم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali quotes the Prophet: legal orphanhood ends at puberty, and a fast is not to be maintained in silence until night.
rows.anchor: عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، قال: حفظت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يتم بعد احتلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha and other Companions report that legal responsibility is lifted from a child until puberty, a sleeper until waking, and an insane person until recovery; fifteen is also treated as adulthood from Ibn Umar's battle-age report, which Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz called the distinction between child and adult.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة وغيرها من الصحابة، رضي الله عنهم، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "رفع القلم عن ثلاثة: عن الصبي حتى يحتلم

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz treated Ibn Umar's admission to battle at fifteen, after rejection at fourteen, as the distinction between minor and adult.
rows.anchor: فقال أمير المؤمنين عمر بن عبد العزيز -لما بلغه هذا الحديث -إن هذا الفرق بين الصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Of three views on pubic hair as a sign of puberty, Ibn Kathir rejects distinguishing Muslim boys from protected non-Muslim boys and holds the sign applies to both because it is natural and artificial removal is unlikely.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنها بلوغ في حق الجميع لأن هذا أمر جبلي يستوي فيه الناس

rows.speaker: عطية القرظي
rows.claim: Atiyya al-Qurazi reports that captives of Qurayza were examined: those with pubic hair were killed, while those without it were released; he was among those released.
rows.anchor: عن عطية القرظي، رضي الله عنه قال: عرضنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم قريظة فكان من أنبت قتل

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: The Qurayza puberty report is transmitted in all four Sunan collections; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih, reflecting Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's ruling to kill combatants and enslave their offspring.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي: حسن صحيح. وإنما كان كذلك؛ لأن سعد بن معاذ، رضي الله عنه، كان قد حكم فيهم بقتل المقاتلة وسبي الذرية.

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report says Umar examined a boy accused of falsely claiming sexual relations with a girl, found no pubic hair, and dropped the penalty.
rows.anchor: عن عمر: أن غلاما ابتهر جارية في شعره، فقال عمر، رضي الله عنه: انظروا إليه.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd explains ibtihār as falsely claiming sex, while ibtiyār means the claim is true; al-Kumayt's verse witnesses the distinction between the two words.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: ابتهرها: أي قذفها، والابتهار (3) أن يقول: فعلت بها وهو كاذب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and other authorities explain discernment as sound religion and protection of wealth; jurists end guardianship when a boy reaches puberty with these qualities.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: يعني: صلاحا في دينهم وحفظا لأموالهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians are forbidden to consume orphan property wastefully or hastily before the orphans reach adulthood, unless there is a necessary need.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ولا تأكلوها إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا} ينهى تعالى عن أكل أموال اليتامى من غير حاجة ضرورية

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says a wealthy guardian must abstain from orphan property as from carrion and blood.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي: هو عليه كالميتة والدم.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the allowance concerns an orphan's guardian who manages and improves the estate and is needy; he may eat a customary amount proportionate to his work.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: أنزلت هذه الآية في والي اليتيم {ومن كان غنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists cap a needy guardian's draw at the lesser of a fair wage for the work or the amount needed.
rows.anchor: قال الفقهاء: له أن يأكل أقل الأمرين: أجرة مثله أو قدر حاجته.

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: One view requires no repayment if the guardian later becomes solvent; al-Shafi'i's companions prefer it because the verse permits eating without requiring compensation.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الصحيح عند أصحاب الشافعي؛ لأن الآية أباحت الأكل من غير بدل.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man without assets who has an orphan asks about using the orphan's wealth; the Prophet permits customary, non-wasteful use, without hoarding or shielding one's own property at the orphan's expense.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده: أن رجلا سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ليس لي مال ولي يتيم؟

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second version answers that a guardian with nothing may eat from the orphan's estate in customary measure, without excess.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن عندي يتيما عنده مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second juristic position requires a guardian to repay what he consumed once solvent, treating the allowance as a necessary loan from property normally protected from use.
rows.anchor: والثاني: نعم؛ لأن مال اليتيم على الحظر، وإنما أبيح للحاجة، فيرد بدله كأكل مال الغير للمضطر

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says he treated himself like an orphan's guardian: he abstained when wealthy, borrowed from the public treasury when in need, and repaid after becoming solvent; Ibn Kathir calls al-Bara's chain authentic.
rows.anchor: عن حارثة بن مضرب قال: قال عمر [بن الخطاب] (9) رضي الله عنه: إني أنزلت نفسي من هذا المال بمنزلة والي اليتيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets eating according to recognized fair measure as taking a loan from the orphan's wealth; Ubayda, Abu al-Aliya, Abu Wa'il, one report from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi are also cited for this view.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} يعني: القرض.

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah, Ikrima, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Atiyya al-Awfi, and al-Hasan hold that the guardian need not repay the customary amount consumed.
rows.anchor: وبهذا القول -وهو عدم أداء البدل (8) -يقول عطاء بن أبي رباح، وعكرمة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A second report from Umar tells al-Bara that a needy guardian may take from the public funds but must restore it when able, and abstain if self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: عن البراء قال: قال لي عمر، رضي الله عنه: إني أنزلت نفسي من مال الله بمنزلة والي اليتيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a poor guardian may take from the estate for his own upkeep so he does not need to draw on the orphan's funds; Mujahid, Maymun ibn Mihran, and al-Hakam are also cited for this interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف} قال: يأكل من ماله، يقوت على يتيمه

rows.speaker: عامر الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi allows consumption only under dire need like eating carrion and requires repayment.
rows.anchor: وقال عامر الشعبي: لا يأكل منه إلا أن يضطر إليه، كما يضطر إلى [أكل] (4) الميتة، فإن أكل منه قضاه.

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Rabi'a say the verse allows spending on the poor orphan according to his poverty, with nothing for the guardian; Ibn Kathir rejects this as distant from context, where rich and poor refer to guardians.
rows.anchor: قال: سألت يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري وربيعة عن قول الله: {فليأكل بالمعروف} فقالا (5) ذلك في اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linked rule is to approach orphan wealth only in the best manner until adulthood; a guardian in need may use it only fairly and for proper care.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد من السياق؛ لأنه قال: {ومن كان غنيا فليستعفف} يعني: من الأولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the orphan reaches puberty and discernment, the guardian must hand over the estate and have the recipient's receipt witnessed to prevent later denial.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {فإذا دفعتم إليهم أموالهم} يعني: بعد بلوغهم الحلم وإيناس الرشد [منهم] (7) فحينئذ سلموهم أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sufficient as accountant, witness, and watcher over guardians, knowing whether they preserve the full estate or diminish it through concealed accounting and deception.
rows.anchor: أي: وكفى بالله محاسبا وشهيدا ورقيبا على الأولياء في حال نظرهم للأيتام، وحال تسليمهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns Abu Dharr, whom he considers weak, not to take command over two people or manage an orphan's property.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يا أبا ذر، إني أراك ضعيفا، وإني أحب لك ما أحب لنفسي، لا تأمرن على اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying encounter with God lose and will suddenly regret wasted deeds and their prior bad actions when the Hour arrives.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن خسارة من كذب بلقاء الله وعن خيبته إذا جاءته الساعة بغتة، وعن ندامته على ما فرط من العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the regret about what was neglected may refer to worldly life, deeds, or the afterlife and its affairs.
rows.anchor: وهذا الضمير يحتمل عوده على الحياة [الدنيا] (7) وعلى الأعمال، وعلى الدار الآخرة، أي: في أمرها.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The wording about carrying burdens means carrying them; Qatada also glosses the verb as working or earning.
rows.anchor: وقوله {وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون} أي: يحملون. وقال قتادة: يعملون.

rows.speaker: أبو مرزوق
rows.claim: Abu Marzuq describes a wicked person meeting an ugly, foul-smelling embodiment of his evil deeds at resurrection; it rides him toward Hell, illustrating the burdens on their backs.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مرزوق قال: ويستقبل الكافر -أو: الفاجر - (9) -عند خروجه من قبره كأقبح صورة رآها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says an unjust dead person is accompanied in the grave by an ugly, black, stinking figure that embodies his deeds; at resurrection he carries it toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال أسباط: عن السدي أنه قال: ليس من رجل ظالم يموت فيدخل قبره إلا جاءه رجل قبيح الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most worldly life is play and amusement, while the abode of the hereafter is better for those who fear God; people should reflect.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو} أي: إنما غالبها كذلك {وللدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's people argued about monotheism with sophistry, but he asks how they can dispute after God opened his sight and guided him to the truth; their false claims deserve no attention.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى: وجادله قومه فيما ذهب إليه من التوحيد، وناظروه بشبه من القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's refusal to fear their gods proves their claims false: if the idols can act, let them plot and hasten their harm.
rows.anchor: فإن كان لها صنع، فكيدوني بها [جميعا] (1) ولا تنظرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception about God's will is disconnected: nothing harms or benefits except God alone.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا} استثناء منقطع. أي لا يضر ولا ينفع إلا الله، عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge encompasses every thing, and no hidden matter escapes Him.
rows.anchor: {وسع ربي كل شيء علما} أي: أحاط علمه بجميع الأشياء، فلا تخفى (2) عليه خافية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to remember means considering Abraham's explanation, recognizing the idols' falsehood, and abandoning their worship.
rows.anchor: {أفلا تتذكرون} أي: فيما بينته (3) لكم فتعتبرون أن هذه الآلهة باطلة، فتزجروا (4) عن عبادتها؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's argument parallels Hud's challenge to Aad: he disavowed their idols and challenged them to plot against him while trusting God, as narrated in Hud.
rows.anchor: وهذه الحجة نظير ما احتج به نبي الله هود، عليه السلام، على قومه عاد، فيما قص عنهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities explain the absent divine authority as proof: Abraham asks how people fear powerless idols while failing to fear their unsupported association of partners with God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغير واحد من السلف: أي حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses likewise deny any divinely authorized basis for associating partners or inventing religious law.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله} [الشورى: 21]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The safer party is the one worshipping the God who controls harm and benefit, rather than powerless beings worshipped without proof; the question concerns safety from God's punishment at resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي: فأي الطائفتين أصوب؟ الذي عبد من بيده الضر والنفع، أو الذي عبد من لا يضر ولا ينفع بلا دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe without mixing faith with shirk devote worship to God alone; they are secure on Judgment Day and guided in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: أي: هؤلاء الذين أخلصوا العبادة لله وحده لا شريك، له، ولم يشركوا به شيئا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the verse troubled the Companions, the Prophet clarified through Luqman's words that the injustice meant here is shirk, not every sin or wrong against oneself.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: يا رسول الله، فأينا لا يظلم نفسه؟ (5) قال: "إنه ليس الذي تعنون!

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet was told: You are among those described by it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: لما نزلت: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "قيل لي: أنت منهم"

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jarir narrates a traveler who accepts the Prophet's basic teachings, dies when his camel falls into a rodent hole, and is described as one with little work but great reward; angels place Paradise's fruit in his mouth because he died hungry, and the Prophet directs that he be buried in a niche.
rows.anchor: ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "هذا من الذين قال الله، عز وجل: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم}

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second Jarir route repeats the traveler story and the Prophet's description of the man as having done little yet earned much.
rows.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله، فذكر نحوه، وقال فيه: "هذا ممن عمل قليلا وأجر كثيرا"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a Bedouin who leaves home, possessions, and family seeking the Prophet's guidance, accepts Islam, and dies in an accidental fall; the Prophet affirms his sincere quest and says he is among those secure and guided without shirk.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسير (2) ساره، إذ عرض له أعرابي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Umar describes the secure and guided as those who respond to favor with gratitude, deprivation with patience, personal wrongdoing with seeking forgiveness, and injury with pardon.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أعطي فشكر ومنع فصبر وظلم فاستغفر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says anyone wanting to read the Prophet's sealed written testament should recite the An'am verses beginning here through the closing command to be mindful.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: من أراد أن يقرأ صحيفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التي عليها خاتمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the An'am passages here decisive verses and foundations of scripture, then recites this commandment.
rows.anchor: قال: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: في (2) الأنعام آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports that the Prophet took a pledge on three matters, reciting these prohibitions: the faithful receive reward, breaches may be punished in this life, and those deferred to the next rest with God, who may punish or forgive. Al-Hakim grades it authentic, though Bukhari and Muslim transmit only the shorter pledge; Ibn Kathir says Sufyan may preserve both reports.
rows.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أيكم يبايعني على ثلاث؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to address polytheists who worship others, forbid God's provision, and kill children under Satan's prompting: come hear what God truly forbade by revelation, not conjecture.
rows.anchor: وأما تفسيرها فيقول تعالى لنبيه ورسوله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: قل يا محمد -لهؤلاء المشركين الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening prohibition omits an understood phrase, 'and He commanded you'; the verse's conclusion and an Arabic poetic example support this ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وكأن في الكلام محذوفا دل عليه السياق، وتقديره: وأوصاكم (1) {ألا تشركوا به شيئا}

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports Gabriel's assurance that a member of the Prophet's community who dies without associating partners with God enters Paradise even if guilty of adultery, theft, or drinking wine; a variant has the Prophet add despite Abu Dharr's displeasure.
rows.anchor: من حديث أبي ذر، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أتاني جبريل فبشرني أنه من مات لا يشرك بالله شيئا من أمتك، دخل الجنة

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In a sacred report to Abu Dharr, God promises forgiveness to one who invokes and hopes in Him, even with earthful sins, provided the person does not associate partners with Him; sincere later repentance is also forgiven.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر [رضي الله عنه] (6) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يقول الله تعالى: يا ابن آدم، إنك ما دعوتني ورجوتني فإني أغفر لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an 4:48 and 4:116 says God does not forgive shirk but may forgive lesser sins; Ibn Mas'ud's report likewise promises Paradise to one who dies without shirk, and many other texts support this.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى (8) : {إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء}

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports from Ubadah and Abu al-Darda command believers not to associate partners with God even if burned, cut, or crucified; Ubadah also lists this as the first of seven counsels.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن مردويه من حديث عبادة وأبي الدرداء: "لا تشركوا بالله شيئا، وإن قطعتم أو صلبتم أو حرقتم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command concerning parents means God commands people to treat them excellently, as reiterated in Isra'.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وبالوالدين إحسانا} أي: وأوصاكم وأمركم بالوالدين إحسانا، أي: أن تحسنوا إليهم

rows.speaker: reader
rows.claim: Some readers use the variant 'wa-waṣṣā rabbuka' (your Lord commanded), supporting the construction of the preceding command.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم: "ووصى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture often pairs obedience to God with kindness to parents; even when parents are polytheists, one should treat them well without obeying their call to shirk, as in Luqman and the Israelite covenant.
rows.anchor: كما قال: {أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير * وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the deeds most loved by God are prayer on time, filial kindness, then striving in God's cause; the Prophet might have named more had Ibn Mas'ud asked.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي العمل أحب إلى الله؟

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Weakly transmitted reports from Abu al-Darda and Ubadah say the Prophet advised obeying parents even if they ordered one to leave all worldly possessions.
rows.anchor: بسنده عن أبي الدرداء، وعن عبادة بن الصامت، كل منهما يقول: أوصاني خليلي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أطع والديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding kindness to parents, God commands care for children; people killed daughters from shame and sometimes sons from fear of poverty, under satanic temptation.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا يقتلون أولادهم كما سولت لهم الشياطين ذلك، فكانوا يئدون البنات خشية العار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet ranking associating partners with God as the greatest sin, followed by killing a child from fear of sharing food and then adultery with a neighbor's wife; he recited the parallel list in Furqan.
rows.anchor: قلت: يا رسول الله، أي الذنب أعظم؟ قال: "أن تجعل لله ندا وهو خلقك". قلت: ثم أي؟ قال: "أن تقتل ولدك خشية أن يطعم معك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Suddi gloss poverty as present destitution; by contrast, 17:31 forbids killing children for fear of future poverty and puts their provision first, while this verse addresses current poverty and puts parents first.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة، والسدي: هو الفقر، أي: ولا تقتلوهم من فقركم الحاصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on manifest and hidden indecencies parallels the comprehensive prohibition in A'raf and the earlier call to leave outward and inward sin.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى: {قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet saying no one is more jealous than God, and because of His jealousy He forbade both open and hidden indecencies.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا أحد أغير من الله، من أجل ذلك حرم الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Sa'd ibn Ubada threatened a man he found with his wife, the Prophet said he was more jealous than Sa'd and God more jealous than he; that divine jealousy is why indecencies are forbidden.
rows.anchor: فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: "أتعجبون من غيرة سعد! فوالله لأنا أغير من سعد، والله أغير مني

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra likewise says God is jealous and forbids indecencies; Ibn Mardawayh alone transmits it, though Ibn Kathir says this chain matches one used for another report.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قيل: يا رسول الله، إنا (4) . نغار. قال: "والله إني لأغار، والله أغير مني، ومن غيرته نهى عن الفواحش"
